listing.name: Finer Ship Collisions
listing.summary: Updates collision models and reduces collision radii for vanilla ships to improve navigation and consistency.
listing.aiSummary: Updates collision models and reduces collision radii for vanilla ships to improve navigation and consistency.

description:
Starsector is a game which clearly has evolved over time, this is something which is seen when looking at its ship files, where elements which aren't as visible to the players, such as the ships collision models, generated through the assigned ship points leaves a bit to be desired. With inconsistently applied logic when it comes to what should be considered solid and not, some inefficiencies, other ugliness. This has sadly also affected mod developers, as the vanilla games ships often serve as poor role-models.

INFO

The core of this mod serves 2 purposes:

Collision Models

Firstly, to update the collision models for some of the ships, for the reasons discussed above.

Collision Radius

Secondly to address another concern, namely the large collision radii (a parameter separate from collision models, most notably used in ship navigation in combat).

Collisions in the vanilla game are large, typically extending a great distance outside the visual ship, especially so for large ships, often resulting in routing becoming exceedingly annoying when your fleet (or the enemies) is forced to cluster together, making the ships unable to navigate around one another, despite there seemingly being plenty of space to do so.

This is however done for a very specific reason, namely reduce the visual overlap between the engine exhaust, or the shield, of a ship and other ships. While this is inconsistency applied in the vanilla game, and some mods do not attempt to reduce this whatsoever, and while this change will improve the gameplay experience, some increase in this form of visual awkwardness is inevitable, making this change somewhat more subjective. (It should also be noted that some buffer is typically kept.)

Shields

On top of the above mentioned changes, some tweaks to shield radii and centering were made, as some ships had their shields balanced in the rear, or were just a little awkward, presumably for similar reasons as how the collision radii are handled. These changes should be mostly unnoticeable to the average player.

Download Link

Download Here

(Please make sure this mod is loaded before any other mods which overwrite vanilla ships.)

Changelog

Code

- Adjustments and more thoughtful point placement, some ships have reduced points while some have had some points added, for a finer set of collision models, which are more consistent and accurate. Should have generally very slight negative performance impact, depending on fleet loadouts, with a lot of wastefulness reduced, but with some added collision complexity to select mid-size to larger ships.
- Fixed most minor mirroring issues.
- Fixed centering issues.
- Reduced most collision radiuses across the board.
- Very minor shield tweaks, mostly some centering, but also some slight radius reductions when recentering permitted

Known issues:

- If any of the vanilla ships are overridden by other mods, the game has a tendency to load in elements from both mods rather than selecting one of them. This should be able to be avoided by physically overwriting the hull files in the starsector-core/data folder. If doing this, make sure to back up the hull folder before overwriting.

- As mentioned in the collision radii section, this mod will cause more situations where engine exhaust or particle effects overlap with adjacent ships, there isn't really a way to fix this, other than perhaps maintaining 2 versions of the mod, with and without my radii changes, which I have no current plans of doing. Do however message me with pictures if there is any particularly egregious examples.

Make sure to report any issues not mentioned above if you encounter them.

Mods

Fun fact, this mod did not actually start as an improvement mod to vanilla ships. But rather as an attempt to fix the various issues found across the various mods available out here. Then, as I went through all mods, making sure they all followed the same logic, I eventually moved to make the same changes to the vanilla game, resulting in this rather massively time consuming project.

Info

Probably the most autistic thing I've done.

Like mentioned previously, the vanilla game isn't necessarily a great role model, being somewhat internally inconsistent with what it considers solid. This has resulted in a modding landscape with a pretty large difference between how ships are handled from mod to mod. With both how precise the collision model should be, what elements should collide, and how far into the ships sprite the collision should occur, varying greatly.

While my refinements to these mods, does also fix a lot of issues, present in a majority of the mods, ranging from small issues such as incorrect mirroring, to collision models copied wholesale from other ships, resulting in completely inaccurate collision, the core idea is to make the collision handling consistent. While some may disagree with any particular decision I have made regarding the collision, how precise it should be, or what should be part of the collision model, the point is that these decisions are now internally consistent all across ever mod present here, as well as the vanilla ships. Resulting in a more predictable experience.

My changes to these ships, also include my philosophy regarding collision radius, namely to prioritize smaller collision radii, which does not include effects, prioritizing gameplay experience, over mitigating potential awkwardness. (Since modders often handle these in very different ways, the collision radii are instead increased in some mods, to prevent sprite overlapping, and maintaining a small buffer.)

These typically also include larger changes to shields than those made to the vanilla game, often times prevent shields from overlapping weapons, where the mod authors did not take it into account (a pretty common issue), but does also include some personal adjustments to remove perceived weirdness. Faction mods were typically adjusted less so than mods which adds individual ships, to maintain the authorial intent of the authors. While these changes should be relatively invisible, if you find yourself disagreeing with any specific change I have made, do let me know.

As with any mod I create, feel free to do with these modifications as you wish, no credit to me needed, whether that is to incorporate them, either wholesale or in part into any mod or fork, or redistribute them. Although letting me know would of course be appreciated.
If you as a mod author want me to remove my changes available for your specific mod, please do let me know, and they will be removed.
If any part of the moderation team notices that any specific change goes against a modders known wishes, which I may have overlooked (which is very possible given how many mods this tackles), please do remove the download link associated with the given mod.

Installation instructions

Unlike the main mod, the affected .ship files are not provided as a separate mod, due to conflict reasons.

Instead you need to go into the mod-folder for the given mod, then navigate to

"NameofModFolder"\data\hulls/

and and overwrite all ship files with the ones provided by this mod.

Please make sure that the version of the files here correspond with the version of the mod they are installed to, if the author changes the weapon loadout of any of the ships between versions, this will result in a crash when the ships are loaded.

Links

The required mods are not provided here.

"version": "1.5a"
Changelog

-Fixed 1 incorrect collision point assignment

-General reduction and smarter use of points for most ships, should be more accurate, while also being more performant

"version":"v 0.1"

"version":"1.4e"
Changelog

SpoilerHad really simplistic collisions, which isn't necessarily bad, but by adding just a few more points, collision models are vastly improved, especially for the larger ships.

-Added a few more points to adhere a bit more accurately to the very uneven surfaces of the ships.

-Reduced collision radii of some ships.[close]

BigBeans Ship Compilation

"version":"0.1.98.85"
Changelog

SpoilerAlready had pretty decent collision points (really nice seeing), but savings could still be pretty easily gained. Radiuses were pretty inconsistently applied

-General reduction and smarter use of points for most ships, should be more accurate, while also being more performant. (Although the marauder ended up with 1 singular point more than it started out with in this particular case)

-Reduced collision radius of some ships

-Fixed some miss-aligned shields

-Reduced the shield radius of some low-tech ships with very oversized shields to more sensible numbers.[close]

Carter's Freetraders

"version": "3.2.4"
Changelog

SpoilerI suspect these may have been created in a text editor without a visual aid, because these had some really rough bounds. As you all know, and as most of my patches are testament to, it is good to reduce the number of bounds for performance reasons. But, uh, maybe a cruiser needs more than a single square. (No, I'm not talking about the square ship, that one had 8 points lol)

- Added some more points to the collision bounds, still keeping it a fair bit below most other mods, since I didn't want too big of a jump. Drastically improved accuracy, but if you are really struggling in battles, do be aware.

- That being said, some hulls could also be trimmed down a bit, reducing their collision points.

- Downsized a lot of really oversized collision bounds. TBH, this is what you would probably have noticed most.

- A lot of collisions were strangely unsymmetrical, this has been fixed

- Adjusted collision radius and position, generally downsizing them.

- Recentered a few shields slightly.[close]
